algorithm: Full-depth minimax tic-tac-toe with center-first deterministic move order
complexity: O(b^d) minimax per move; trivial for a 3x3 board
data_flow_ascii:
new_board -> play_game(x_move, o_move) -> move functions
minimax(board, player) -> (score, best_move) each turn
winner(board) -> X / O / draw / None -> rendered final board + tally
description_sentence: A playable tic-tac-toe game with an unbeatable minimax AI: scripted AI-vs-AI demo by default, interactive play with --play.
failure_note: Illegal moves raise ValueError in scripted play; interactive mode re-prompts instead of crashing, and 'q' quits cleanly.

label: terminal game
output_shape: Prints each scripted game's final board, winner, and move count, plus an overall win/draw tally.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} with an unbeatable AI opponent that you can watch play itself or challenge directly.

qa.a: Tic-tac-toe is fully solved and tiny: full-depth minimax explores the whole game tree in milliseconds, so no pruning is needed.
qa.q: Why full-depth minimax instead of a heuristic?

qa.a: Ties are broken by the fixed MOVE_ORDER (center first), so the AI's choices are identical on every run.
X maximizes (+1 win) and O minimizes (-1 loss); the recursion returns the best achievable score and its move.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with a full-depth minimax AI, scripted demo games, and an interactive play mode.
run_notes: --play enables interactive input() mode; --games sets the number of scripted demo games.
scaling_note: Minimax is fine for 3x3; larger boards would need depth limits or alpha-beta pruning.
storage_note: No persistence: boards and tallies exist only during the run.
tradeoff_note: Pure minimax is simple and provably optimal here, but it would be far too slow for games with bigger branching factors.
